correctness.rationale: The sampling kernel equals (2l+1)P_l(dot), with 12 parity-compatible representatives. Symmetry alternation gives the degree-eight obstruction for every ratio t>1: the only degree-eight polynomial of the required B3-character is r^2 Delta, and its Laplacian is 30 Delta, so no harmonic can carry it. At t=2, exact rational ranks l=0..8 are 1,3,5,6,9,9,10,12,11; the l=8 sign nullity is exactly one. Independent modular determinants are nonzero in each of two primes at every l=9..528, and rational denominator invertibility makes them conclusive. The Laplace Legendre bound and 11-row diagonal dominance cover every l>=529. Determinants as nonzero rational functions of t prove all transcendental parameter assertions. The actual final checker succeeded; the infinite proof is not extrapolated from checks.

value.rationale: The regular truncated octahedron is a canonical 24-point Archimedean orbit; interpolation in one exact harmonic degree is a natural harmonic-sampling problem. Nonmonotone surjectivity at degrees 7,8,9 is not a small numerical improvement: a full data dimension disappears in degree eight despite growing harmonic dimension, and the missing functional is explicitly identified as an intrinsic signed-discriminant character. The obstruction persists for an entire 1-parameter family and perfect recovery holds for all transcendental ratios at every other high degree. The closed all-degree classification, sharp permanent cutoff, and reproducing-kernel reconstruction make the precise result useful beyond an isolated finite table.
